name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 15 points, among the reddest in Arizona
Gosar is an entrenched incumbent with a large cash-on-hand advantage
Sterbinsky has raised a notable sum but holds under $30,000 in the bank
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 4%
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Gosar's incumbency, and his financial advantage outweigh a potentially favorable national environment and Sterbinsky's respectable fundraising total; markets and fundamentals align on a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A major Gosar scandal or a late wave of Democratic outside spending could tighten the race, though the district's lean makes any upset a steep climb.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This northern Arizona seat is one of the most Republican-leaning in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Paul Gosar, a controversial but entrenched incumbent, has won reelection comfortably in every cycle and enters the general election with about $319,000 on hand, far more than his Democratic challenger.

Dani Sterbinsky has raised a respectable $437,000 for a race in a district like this, but reports only about $29,000 in the bank heading into the fall. No public polls cover the contest, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a four percent chance of winning. A national environment favorable to Democrats could trim the margin somewhat, but the district's underlying lean and Gosar's incumbency make a Republican hold the clear expectation.
